narrator.how: the Traveller as an old man, remembering: low, unhurried, plain and warm; short sentences, a little dry humour; never sentimental — the feeling is in the pauses

traveller.how: a young man, curious and talkative, quick and friendly; counts things aloud when he is embarrassed; jokes when refused; goes quiet and short when moved; older in the later chapters, slower and plainer

elzeard.how: an old shepherd who almost never speaks: low, slow, even, a little hoarse; one word or a few, flat as stones, no emphasis; never asks, never thanks; a rare short laugh

lina.how: a village girl, later a woman, from a charcoal burners' hamlet: quick, sharp-tongued and stubborn, laughs first when ashamed, rough when tender; plain country speech; with city people curt and closed

jan.how: a former soldier, then a district forester: dry, terse, matter-of-fact; jokes so dryly it hardly sounds like a joke; writes as he talks; warm underneath, never says so

father.how: a charcoal burner, Lina's father: rough, bitter, shouting, worn out by a hungry life

chief.how: an official from the city: hearty, booming, enthusiastic and pleased with himself; understands nothing and laughs at his own jokes

ranger.how: a young ranger from the city: serious, stiff and by the book, a little self-important

axeman.how: a village man with an axe: gruff, practical, unbothered, a little mocking

visitor.how: a visitor from the city: eager, curious, a little loud, polite
